topic: Motion: Distance, Displacement, Speed, and Velocity
key_concepts: Motion is described by how fast or slow an object moves
Distance is the total path length traveled regardless of direction
Displacement is the change in position with both magnitude and direction
Speed is the distance covered per unit time and is a scalar quantity
Velocity is the displacement per unit time and includes direction
Speed and velocity can have equal magnitude in straight-line motion
Uniform motion is constant speed in a specific direction
Average speed is total distance divided by total time
Average velocity is total displacement divided by total time
Instantaneous speed is the speed at a particular instant
Zero displacement results in zero average velocity
Speed and velocity problems use v=d/t and displacement equals velocity multiplied by time
